content: I hope you received enough feedback from the community to improve your contribution. Once you have made the necessary updates, publish your contribution!
fun

Looks like a fun puzzle! Rules * Optional: consider adding "to" between "move" and "or shoot into" (noting that "to" is used after "move" in the Output section). * Please specify whether two or more features (bats, a shaft, the Mumpus) can occupy the same room. * Please specify whether bats and the Mumpus always remains in their initial rooms or can move during the game. Expert rules * "After transporting you, the bat flies away, leaving the original room unoccupied": what exactly happens to the bat afterwards? • Does it leave the cave entirely? • Does it move to another room? • If so, does it choose an unexplored room or any room at random? • Can it move into a room that already contains a hazard? • If it prefers unexplored safe rooms, what happens when none remain? My assumption is that the bat simply leaves the cave, but it'd be helpful to state this explicitly. * Optional: consider adding "to" between "move" and "or shoot into" here as well. Input * Please add "space-separated" after each of the three occurrences of "Three". Input for a game round * Please add line numbers, for example: Line 1: One integer (etc.) Similarly for Lines 2 and 3. * Please add "the room IDs of" before "the three adjacent rooms". * For the clue inputs, please add ", 0 otherwise" to each description. Output * Please change "One command" to "One of the following commands". * Please format "MOVE" and "SHOOT" using the tag instead of . * Please format "roomId" using the tag instead of . Constraints * Please format all variable names using the tag. * Optional: it'd be helpful to specify the range of valid room IDs (0 to roomCount - 1?). * Please specify that the starting room is always safe and free of bats. * If solvability is guaranteed, please state that every case can be solved without guessing. Stub generator * Interesting; I didn't know it was possible to include a variable directly in a write statement. How did you write that? Cases, viewer and error messages * I'll review these once the above points have been addressed. Thanks.

OK. I believe I have addressed those comments and added a few other clarifications.
Here is my stub:
```
read roomCount:int batCount:int shaftCount:int

gameloop
read currentRoom:int
read roomA:int roomB:int roomC:int
read bats:int shaft:int mumpus:int

write join("MOVE", roomA)

OUTPUT
MOVE roomId | SHOOT roomId
```

Thanks for the stub generator code. I wasn't aware that defined variables could be used directly in a write statement.

Also, thank you for updating the statement. The revision has resolved most ambiguities.

Rules
* Please apply the bullet-point format to the items that aren't currently formatted so.

* The final sentence appears to imply that some cases may be random and could require guessing. Could you clarify?

* I assume no guessing should be needed. If so, consider removing "non-random" and adding "are non-random and" after "validators".

Expert Rules
* Point 1: Please remove "preferably one" and add "if any exists" at the end.

* Please change "caves" to "cave" (twice).

* Optional: consider adding "to" between "move" and "or shoot into" here (noting that "to" is used after "move" in the Output section).

* Consider mentioning the option to toggle room numbers in the viewer.

Input
* Please change "your current room number" to "the room ID of your current room" for consistency.

Output
* Please use line breaks in a consistent style in the descriptions of MOVE and SHOOT.

Constraints
* Please remove the final two constraints (they'll be moved to a new "Defeat conditions" section, see below).

* Please format all variable names using the <var> tag.

* Please add (with <var> tags):
batsCount + shaftsCount + 5 < roomCount

  (The 5 accounts for the Mumpus room, the starting room, and the three rooms adjacent to the starting room.)

* Please add (with <var> tags):
0 <= roomId < roomCount

  (Sorry for the confusion by describing this as optional in my previous comment).

* Please state that all <var>roomId</var>s are distinct.

Input / Constraints / Stub generator
* Please standardise variable names:
  • batsCount vs batCount
  • shaftsCount vs shaftCount
  • a vs roomA
  • b vs roomB
  • c vs roomC

Victory / Defeat conditions
* Please insert these two sections before the Expert Rules. The source code of this page includes an example of the HTML code to use: https://www.codingame.com/ide/puzzle/flames-extinguisher

Cases
* The shuffled-room-number cases (Tiny Validator, Medium Validator, Dodecahedron - Classic, and Tiny Hard Validator) don't provide adjacent room IDs in ascending order.

* Are these the only cases that use shuffled room numbers? If so, may I suggest adding more such cases in both fixed and random tests and validators?

* Could the cases include a greater variety of hazard counts? Currently, the bat count is usually 1 or 2 (except for two tests with 10 bats), while the shaft count is always between 0 and 3. There are cases with no shafts, but none with no bats.

* What are the main differences between the "Classic - Random Bats" and "Classic - Crazy Bats" tests?

* If there are no major differences, please convert one of the tests into a validator, as no validator covers the scenario with 10 bats.

Referee
* Outputting "MOVE 9" or "MOVE -1" (or SHOOT instead of MOVE) causes Test 1 to crash (out-of-bounds error).

Thanks.

I'm not sure whether you've finished updating the puzzle, but below is the current list of outstanding items:

Rules
* Please fix the bullet-point formatting in the fifth-last point.

Expert Rules
* In the first bullet point, please remove "preferably one" and add "if any exists" at the end.

* Consider mentioning the option to toggle room numbers in the viewer.

* Consider moving the final part ("Each turn, you must decide … you only have one arrow.") to the Goal section. It seems more natural to tell players upfront that they only have one arrow, before later explaining that shooting it into the wrong room results in defeat.

Loss Conditions
* "Unrecognized command" and "Attempt to act on non-adjacent room" are two distinct loss conditions. Please split them into separate bullet points.

* Please add "Timeout" as a loss condition.

Input
* Please change "roomId" to "room ID".

Output
* Please use line breaks in a consistent style in the descriptions of MOVE and SHOOT. For example, you could add a line break after "into an adjacent room.".

Constraints
* In the final constraint, please change the second "<=" to "<".

* Please add (with <var> tags):
batsCount + shaftsCount + 5 < roomCount

  (The 5 accounts for the Mumpus room, the starting room, and the three rooms adjacent to the starting room.)

Input / Constraints / Stub
* Please standardise the variable names:
  • batsCount vs batCount
  • shaftsCount vs shaftCount

Cases
* Could the cases include a greater variety of hazard counts? Currently, the bat count is usually 1 or 2 (except for two tests with 10 bats), while the shaft count is always between 0 and 3. There are cases with no shafts, but none with no bats.

* What are the main differences between the "Classic - Random Bats" and "Classic - Crazy Bats" tests?

* If there are no major differences, please convert one of the tests into a validator, as no validator covers the scenario with 10 bats.

Thanks.

I fixed a few things but I'm still working on it.
I plan to redo some of the levels, add some more, and rename them.
Noted with thanks!

I believe I've addressed these concerns. Let me know if I missed anything.
I did not add the line about the number of bats being less than the number of rooms. I think that's pretty obvious.
I did not add anything about timeouts since I didn't do anything special with the time limits; I'm just using the defaults.

Added and removed levels and gave them more consistent names.
I think we're getting pretty close final draft.

I love the opening animation and the skull background in the viewer!

Rules
* Please fix the bullet-point formatting in the fifth-last point.

Credits
* Please insert a blank line above the "Credits" heading.

Expert Rules
* Consider swapping the order of the final two bullet points. The cave's connectivity and topology are closely related, so they read more naturally together.

* Consider moving the final part ("Each turn, you must decide … you only have one arrow.") into the Goal section. It seems more natural to tell players upfront that they only have one arrow, before later explaining that shooting it into the wrong room results in defeat. As it stands, those two sentences also feel slightly out of place because they aren't part of any section.

Loss Conditions
* Please add "Timeout" as a loss condition. A solution can time out because of an infinite loop or failing to produce output. Even if you're using the default time limits, a timeout is still a loss condition and should be listed.

Input
* Please change "roomId" to "room ID".

Output
* SHOOT: Please add a line break after "into an adjacent room." to match the formatting you used for MOVE.

Cases
* Crazy Bats (test) and Crazy Bats (V) (validator) violate the constraint on batsCount.

* There are now 19 tests and 10 validators. Please revise the test suite so that there are equal numbers of tests and validators, with each test paired with a corresponding validator covering the same scenario.

For example, there's currently one PENTAGONS FIXED test and six RANDOM tests, but no corresponding validators for those scenarios.

Viewer
* When room numbers are enabled in the viewer, some are partially obscured by the player, bat, shaft or Mumpus icons, making the numbers difficult to read. A few possible improvements are:

  • Draw the room numbers on top of the icons.
  • Use a font colour that contrasts better with the icons.
  • Add a semi-transparent background behind the room numbers to improve readability.

Thanks.

Thank you for the feedback.
Those all sound reasonable. I will continue working on it.
Regarding Random levels: they are randomly generated each time you play.
This is mostly to give the players a chance to have fun and play the game with a large variety of maps.
I'm not sure a Random map makes sense as a "Validator".
What do you think?
I agree that all of the other maps should have at least one validator.
Thank you for your explanation. I agree with you.

You can see the room numbers (and the hazards) with tooltips by hovering your mouse over them.
Maybe I should mention that?
Yes, I knew that, but it's still a good idea to mention that.

New version uploaded:

I've put in everything I was planning to add.
If it looks good to you @5DN1L, I'll enable voting on it.

I'd really like to say we're almost there, but unfortunately I haven't been able to review the cases yet (more on that below). There are also a few remaining points on the statement. Hopefully these should be fairly quick to address.

Rules
* The current rule on clues could be read as implying that the input provides the listed phrases as clues. Please revise it to clarify that the actual clues provided as input are <const>0</const> and <const>1</const> values.

* If you'd still like to keep the descriptive phrases, please clarify that the input does not contain these phrases, and that they're only displayed in the console. Please also remove the quotation marks around the three clues, and instead format them using the <const> tag.

* Consider adding "on their own" after "None of the hazards will ever move to a different room". Bats do move when they carry "you" to another room, but they don't move to another room on their own.

Expert Rules
* The first 4 points alternate between "bat" and "bats"; please use one consistently. If you prefer to use "bats", please also change "It" to "They" in the first point.

* Please swap the order of the final two points. The cave's connectivity and topology are closely related, so they read more naturally together. Also, the viewer setting is the only point that isn't really a game rule, so it'd make sense to leave it at the end.

Cases
* I haven't reviewed the cases yet because some validators share the same name, which makes it difficult for me to distinguish between them (the JSON order also differs from the order shown in the IDE). Could you rename the cases so that all tests have distinct names and all validators have distinct names?

It's fine for a test and a validator to have the same name; I can distinguish those easily. The main issue is having duplicate names within the tests or within the validators.

* Some names contain two closing brackets.

Thanks.

Good points. I've done a big pass on the levels.
* all levels have names
* they are ordered from small to big and easy to hard
* the first "must use bats" level is now #8 "Leap of Faith"
Overall, there are 6 basic levels and 8 more advanced ones. There are 2 validators for each. (14*2=28 total). A validator is the same map with the room numbers swapped, though swapping room numbers also changes the bat random drop room.
There are 6 randomly generated levels that do not have validators.

The update is good. I really like the new level structure and progression.

I noticed a few remaining points:

Rules
* Please add "console" before "message".

* Please format the three console messages using the <const> tag.

Expert rules
* First point: Please change "It" to "They".

Input
* Please format the six clue values (0s and 1s) using the <const> tag.

Cases
* Why are several map seeds displayed in the console for the Random cases most of the time? For example, when playing "Random Tiny", I got:

Map seed: -311575415
Map seed: -311575414
Map seed: -311575413
Map seed: -311575412
Map seed: -311575411

Should only one map seed be displayed?

* I'm not entirely sure about having the two sets of validators differ only in their room numbering. I wonder whether the v2 validators could additionally rearrange the entities. For example, by making the map a rotational or reflectional symmetry of the corresponding v1 validator.

Thanks.

Made the text changes.
Also fixed some animation glitches.

When I generate a random case, I run it through my solver to make sure it is actually solvable. if not, I increment the seed and try again. should be a pretty rare occurrence, but there was a bug in the case generator. fixed now. it will still print the one seed it uses.

Shuffling room numbers has the same purpose as mirroring/rotating. It foils hard-coded solutions and has a good chance of catching solutions that use guessing, without giving the players anything they haven't already seen.
Some of the maps are asymmetrical and can't be mirrored/rotated, but I don't think we need to.
We don't necessarily need two validators per test. I can get rid of the second one if you think it's redundant.

Thank you for the update.

I now see only one map seed for each Random case instead of several, so that looks good.

Yes, I think it's fine to remove the second set of validators. My earlier suggestion about rearranging the entities was specifically intended to make the second set meaningfully different from the first and not redundant.
Removed second set of validators.
